plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-11 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Anthropology program page and its linked official degree map, 'Anthropology Degree Maps (2026-2027)', 'Anthropology (Campus)' tab, last updated/reviewed July 31, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Collected as the BS: the program is a combined BA/BS and the map expressly states that students electing the BA take 16 credits of one foreign language, which are not included in the map; the BS version is recorded, following the prior-wave pattern for combined BA/BS programs. The catalog prints Total Credits, BA/BS Degree: 120 (punctuation normalized), which the map matches exactly. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (14/16/15/15/15/15/15/15) and the plan to 120. The catalog prints the Anthropology Curriculum as 37 credits (Required Core Courses 19 credits plus Elective Courses 18 credits of upper-division Anthropology), and the map places exactly 37 ANTH credits: the six named core courses (16 credits), the 3-credit Core Elective slot (Fall Year 3, one of ANTH 2220, ANTH 3030 or ANTH 3070), and six 3-credit Major Upper-division Elective slots totalling the catalog's 18 elective credits. The map notes that students who select ANTH 2220 as the Core Elective may need to complete 3 additional upper-division elective credits, since ANTH 2220 is a 2000-level course; that conditional note is carried on the Core Elective slot. Per the catalog, all courses must be passed with a C- (1.7) or better to count in the major, students must hold a 2.5 GPA in all ANTH courses, a minimum of 18 credits of Anthropology must be taken at SUU including the capstone, and up to 6 credits of ANTH 4960 may be used toward the elective courses. Catalog titles are recorded where the map shortens them ('Anthropological Theory & Methods').
